name: Burkitts Reef ("Greg's Reef")
shape_type_notes: Not an engineered structure with a designed plan-view template -- Burkitts Reef is a natural basalt headland/rock shelf that was reshaped in place (existing boulders broken down and relocated with a rented excavator) rather than built from new imported material. None of V/delta/chevron/linear/crescent/L/mound describes a natural point/headland reef, so 'other' is used. The polygon below traces the visible natural rock/reef extent read off satellite imagery -- it is NOT a surveyed or designed footprint, and no such footprint has ever been published for this reef (confirmed against our own card, which already states 'No footprint length/width figure found', and against every source checked in this pass).
coords: metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid (approx. the beach access point at the southern end of Bargara Beach, near Bill Fritz Park / Burkitt Street, Bargara); x = alongshore (positive toward north, approximate -- Bargara's coastline trends roughly N-S here; no source gives an exact shoreline azimuth); y = offshore (positive seaward, approximately east into the Coral Sea); shoreline approximated as the line y=0. Because the reef is an attached headland (not a detached structure), much of its landward edge lies at or near y=0.

crest_depth_m.datum: exposed dry basalt at low tide (the condition under which the 1997 excavator work was done); rises to roughly 2.5 m of water depth over the same rock at high spring tide

crest_depth_alt_note: This is not a single engineered crest depth -- Burkitts Reef is an intertidal rock platform whose water cover varies continuously with the tide. No source publishes a fixed crest elevation against a survey datum (e.g. LAT). The 0 m (dry) to ~2.5 m (submerged) range is our own inference from R4's stated ~2.5 m local tide swing, not a direct measurement. Corrected 2026-09-25: an earlier draft of this file also cited R8 for the ~2.5 m figure; R8 (Swellnet, re-fetched) corroborates the 1982/1997 timeline and before/after surf-day counts but does not itself restate a tide-swing number, so it has been removed from this citation. Gemini's file gives the same order-of-magnitude range (0.2-2.5 m) but does not tie it to either of its own two relevant sources.
orientation_notes: Attached headland/point at the southern end of Bargara Beach (near Bill Fritz Park / Burkitt Street) trending roughly NNE-SSW, with its rocky tip projecting seaward (east) into the Coral Sea. Consistently described as a 'right-hand point break' (R1,R3): the wave wraps the point and peels back toward the beach, putting the wave face on the surfer's right as they ride it, which is only possible with the seaward apex/densest boulder mass lying to the north/east of the main takeoff zone. No source gives a precise compass bearing or arm angle -- this description is drawn from (a) the plan shape visible in satellite imagery (see images_relied_on) and (b) Greg Redgard's own 1980 hand-drawn petition sketch, which labels a dense boulder mass 'BURKITTS REEF' at the seaward/outer end of a wedge-shaped point, shows a cleared 'swimmers passage' / 'boat passage' channel along the shoreward side, and marks hazard rocks with 'X' roughly midway along the point -- consistent with the satellite-imagery shape and with the Esplanade/houses/Basin/golf-course landmarks also visible on today's satellite imagery.
materials: Natural volcanic basalt boulders (existing headland rock), reshaped in place -- not new material. ~300 m3 of rock relocated, at least 12 large boulders broken down/repositioned, gaps hand-packed with bricks; some old discarded railway-track iron was also present in the rock and cleared [R1,R3,R4,R6,R8] (all figures already in the verified card; not re-derived here).

images_relied_on.what_it_is: Greg Redgard's own hand-drawn 1980 council petition sketch, headed 'PETITION FOR ROCK REMOVAL' and dated 7/9/1980, labeling the headland 'BURKITTS REEF' -- already listed in our verified card's images array under R1
images_relied_on.what_was_read_off_it: Overall wedge/point shape of the natural reef: a dense boulder mass ('swell builds up here, tripling its size') at the seaward/outer end, a band of diagonal wave-crest marks ('waves break here with rocks obstructing surfer') running down toward the beach, a cleared 'swimmers passage' / 'boat passage' channel on the shoreward side, and hazard rocks marked with 'X' roughly midway along the point. Landmarks (Esplanade, houses, Basin, golf course) match today's satellite imagery, confirming the sketch's orientation. This is a schematic, not-to-scale hand drawing -- no metric dimensions were or could be read off it; it was used only to corroborate plan shape and orientation, not size.

images_relied_on.what_it_is: Construction-era photo (Feb 1997) of the rented Kobelco hydraulic excavator on the basalt boulder shore, with a person standing among the boulders and several rocks marked with white 'X' paint -- already listed in our verified card's images array under R1
images_relied_on.what_was_read_off_it: Confirms individual boulder scale (roughly 0.3-1 m across, judged against the person and excavator) and the 'X'-marking method for hazard rocks, matching the 1980 sketch. This photo is a close-up, ground-level view with no wide scale reference (no scale bar, and the far shoreline extent is not visible), so it was NOT used to estimate the reef's overall length/width/area -- only to corroborate boulder-scale and method, which the card's text sources already establish (~300 m3, 12+ boulders).

open_issues: Burkitts Reef is a natural basalt headland reshaped in place, not an engineered structure -- no source (ours or Gemini's) publishes a plan-view footprint, so every geometric figure in this file (polygon, length, width, area) is our own visual estimate from satellite imagery, not a surveyed or designed footprint. Treat with low confidence.

The boundary of 'the reef' versus the surrounding sandy/rocky shore is inherently fuzzy and was judged by eye from satellite imagery; a different analyst could reasonably draw a materially different polygon of a different size.

Precise reef coordinates are not published (already flagged in our verified card); the lat/lon on the card is Bargara town centre, not the reef itself. The polygon here is in local metres relative to an approximate shoreline origin, not tied to a surveyed lat/lon.
No source gives a compass bearing or numeric arm angle for the point; orientation is qualitative only.

verification.item: Alongshore length ~120 m, seaward width ~46 m, area ~2480 m2 -- precision of the S1 satellite-imagery estimate itself
verification.evidence: Independently attempted a rough re-measurement 2026-09-25 using the built-in browser on the same live Google Maps view: read the on-screen scale bar via the page DOM (confirmed '50 m' = 94.55 CSS px at one zoom level, '100 m' = 125.17 CSS px at another, both internally consistent at ~1.32 m/CSS-px after correcting for the viewport-to-screenshot scale factor) and eyeballed pixel spans across the point. Google Maps' right-click 'measure distance' tool could not be driven reliably through the browser-automation tool (menu clicks were inconsistent), so no exact independent distance readout was obtained. A rough pixel-ruler cross-check gave alongshore/cross-shore spans in the same broad order of magnitude (tens of meters) as 120 m / 46 m, but with too much of my own measurement error (differing choice of shoreline attachment points, curved coastline) to either confirm or refute the specific 120/46/2480 figures more tightly than the ±35-50% uncertainty the draft already states. Per the task's instruction to default to 'unsupported' rather than invent a number, the original L/W/area values are kept unchanged, confidence stays 'low', and this residual imprecision is documented here rather than papered over with false precision.
